meta.title: Supplementary Material — Group-conformal calibration of near-infrared prediction intervals for new seasons, instruments and regions using PLS diagnostics
abstract: Supplementary tables S1–S28 and figures S1–S3. All values are generated from the result files of the accompanying code (run_all.py).

blocks.text: S9. Computing cost

blocks.caption: Table S9. Isolated computing cost per held-out season (mango LOSO, ~70 000 training spectra, one CPU core, mean of three seasons).
blocks.note: method_s and peak_MiB are measured after the shared step (group-wise cross-validation and final PLS fit, shared_setup_s), which every PLS-based method needs. Sources of the memory differences: ORACLE, ASTM-G, G-U-A and G-W-A only sort residuals that already exist (< 6 MiB); GC-D, G-U-D and GC-D+ evaluate T² and Q of every training spectrum under its out-of-group fold model, which requires reconstructing the n × p training matrix in double precision (≈ 70 000 × 103 × 8 bytes ≈ 58 MB, plus the scale-model fit); SCP, WCP and HCP fit an additional PLS model on part of the data; CV+, ASTM-R and R-U-* run a second (random) cross-validation; GPR stores the 1000 × 1000 kernel matrix and its factorisation; bagging stores 25 models.

blocks.caption: Fig. S1. Method-specific computing time (left, log scale) and peak additional memory (right); dashed line: shared group-wise cross-validation and final PLS fit.

blocks.text: S17. Form of the scale model σ(x)

blocks.caption: Table S17. GC-D with alternative scale models (seed 0; group-averaged coverage, interval score and width at nominal 0.90). Families: Poisson quasi-likelihood (default), Gamma, Gaussian with log link, least squares on log|r| (log-normal); features: log T² instead of log(1 + T²), Q not divided by Q̃, an added T² × Q product term; a fit weighted by the group-balanced weights; and either diagnostic alone.

Means over held-out groups; for the log-transformed soil OC the mean interval score and width are dominated by a few back-transformed extreme intervals, so medians over groups are also given.

blocks.text: S26. Synthetic study of single-deployment coverage

Model: y = x'β + b_g + ε with p = 10 features, x ~ N(μ_g, I), group mean μ_g ~ N(0, I), group offset b_g ~ N(0, τ²) and heteroscedastic noise ε ~ N(0, 1 + ‖x‖²/p). A least-squares model fitted on K calibration groups (50 observations each, or log-normally distributed sizes) is deployed on a new group of 200 observations; 1000 deployments per setting. Because the group means μ_g let the model partly fit the offsets of the calibration groups, random-split residuals under-state the error for a new group, as for real spectra. GC-A: leave-one-group-out absolute residuals with group-balanced weights; GC-A+: with the finite-sample point mass.

blocks.caption: Table S26. Coverage attained in one new group (1000 deployments per setting): mean, standard deviation and share of deployments covered more than 0.05 below nominal for random-split calibration (SCP), out-of-group calibration (GC-A) and GC-A with the finite-sample point mass (GC-A+), and the share of finite GC-A+ intervals. Further statistics (10th percentile, between-group share of the variance) in results/revision/simulation_finiteK.csv.

Fig. S3. Synthetic study (τ = 1, balanced groups): (a) mean coverage minus nominal, (b) standard deviation of the coverage in one new group and (c) share of new groups covered more than 0.05 below nominal, as a function of the number of calibration groups K for α = 0.05, 0.10 and 0.20.
